concerns.text: Constitution Principle VII requires R², RMSE, MAE to be reported separately for each stress category (drought, salinity, metal toxicity), but FR-008 only says 'reporting R², RMSE, and MAE for each metabolite'. No FR mandates per-stress-type reporting; add it to FR-008 (or a new FR anchored to US-2).

Three Edge Case behaviors have no backing FR: (1) excluding samples with no environmental match >100km is covered by FR-004, but (2) 'metabolites with near-zero variance should be excluded from modeling' and (3) 'outliers beyond 3 SD capped at 1st/99th percentile' have no FR. Add FRs (anchored to US-1/US-2) or these stated behaviors are unbuildable.

US-1 scenario 3 requires predictors to be standardized (zero mean, unit variance), but FR-005 only mandates kNN imputation and log-transformation of metabolites. Add standardization to FR-005 so the story's acceptance scenario is fully covered.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-008 / SC-003 vs constitution.md Principle VII
concerns.text: FR-008 and SC-003 require metrics 'for each metabolite' only, while Constitution Principle VII mandates R²/RMSE/MAE 'reported separately for each stress category (drought, salinity, metal toxicity)' and forbids a single aggregate metric without demonstrated cross-stress consistency. The spec's evaluation requirements are internally incompatible with the ratified constitution; FR-008/SC-003 should be extended to per-stress-type reporting.

US-1 scenario 3 states 'all predictors are standardized (zero mean, unit variance)', but FR-005 only mandates kNN imputation and log-transformation of metabolites — predictor standardization appears in the story but in no functional requirement. Add it to FR-005 (or a new FR) so story and requirements agree.

Edge case 'Outliers beyond 3 standard deviations should be capped at the 1st/99th percentile' is specified behavior with no corresponding FR; the spec's edge-case section and FR list are inconsistent about whether capping is required. Either add an FR or mark the edge case as guidance.

SC-001 says R² is 'measured against the naïve baseline ... to determine if environmental variables explain substantial variance' — 'substantial variance' is not a pass/fail criterion. State the decision rule (e.g., best-model test R² exceeds the naïve baseline R², or a minimum margin) so an implementer can confirm met-or-not. The idea's R² ≥ 0.6 target exists but is not carried into the SC.

Constitution Principle VII mandates that R², RMSE, MAE be reported separately for each stress category (drought, salinity, metal toxicity). FR-008 and SC-003 only require per-metabolite reporting with no per-stress-type breakdown, so the constitution-mandated evaluation is not verifiable from the current requirements. Add an FR/SC clause requiring per-stress-category metrics.

Constitution Principle VI requires the implementation to 'record the specific grid coordinates and temporal offsets used for each sample' for auditability. FR-004 specifies the matching/exclusion logic but not the recording of the alignment provenance, so this auditable output is untestable as specified. Extend FR-004 (or add an FR) to require persisting matched grid coordinates and temporal offsets per sample.

The edge case 'Outliers beyond 3 standard deviations should be capped at the 1st/99th percentile' is not reflected in any FR, so it is not a checkable requirement. Either fold it into FR-005's preprocessing or accept that it is non-binding guidance.

Constitution Principle VII (in-lens per FR-030) mandates that R², RMSE, and MAE be reported SEPARATELY for each stress category (drought, salinity, metal toxicity). FR-008 only requires metrics 'for each metabolite' with no per-stress-type breakdown. Add per-stress-category reporting to FR-008/US-2.

The idea explicitly specifies the split as 'training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%)'. The spec defers these to [deferred]. Split ratios are a stated design parameter of the source idea, not an empirical value to be measured — the [deferred] convention covers measured quantities, not pre-specified methodology constants. Restore the 70/15/15 ratios (or justify the change).

The idea specifies Elastic Net 'α tuned via grid search'; the spec applies Bayesian optimization (≤30 evaluations) to all three models. This is a small methodological substitution not present in the source idea — either restore grid search for Elastic Net α or note the deviation as a clarifier-surfaced simplification.

FR-002/FR-004 retrieve WorldClim 'monthly temperature, precipitation' for each sample's 'sampling date'. WorldClim provides long-term climatological normals (19 bioclim variables), NOT date-specific observed weather. Aligning a sample's sampling date to WorldClim is a category error: the predictor is the same for all samples at a location regardless of year/season. Either use an actual historical weather product (e.g. ERA5/CHIRPS) or drop the date-matching claim; as written the 'temporal alignment' (Constitution VI) is illusory.

The design stratifies by stress type (drought/salinity/metal toxicity) but stress type is not listed as a predictor, and species, organ/tissue, developmental stage, and study-of-origin are not controlled anywhere. In public metabolomics repositories, metabolite variance is dominated by species and batch/study effects; without including or adjusting for these, any environment→metabolite R² is confounded and uninterpretable. The spec must specify how species/study confounding is handled (e.g. include as covariates, or within-species analysis).

FR-010/SC-002 apply a 'two-sided test' for whether permutation importance differs from zero. Permutation importance (decrease in R² on shuffling) is non-negative by construction, so a two-sided test is ill-posed; and the 95% bootstrap CI already contains the zero-comparison. Specify a one-sided test or rely on the bootstrap CI excluding zero.

FR-008/SC-003 report metrics per metabolite but not per stress category, while Constitution Principle VII mandates per-stress-type reporting before any aggregate metric. Pooling R² across drought/salinity/metal-toxicity samples conflates distinct biological regimes and can mask that environmental drivers explain variance in only one stratum. Add per-stress reporting to FR-008.

Random train/validation/test split (FR-006) on samples drawn from few public studies risks leakage: samples from the same study/species/site appearing in both train and test, inflating out-of-sample R². Specify grouping (e.g. GroupKFold by study or species) for the split.

The idea explicitly specifies the split as 'training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%)'. The spec defers these to [deferred]. Split ratios are a stated design parameter of the source idea, not an empirical value to be measured — the [deferred] convention covers measured quantities, not pre-specified methodology constants. Restore the 70/15/15 ratios (or justify the change).
